title: The Unquiet Parish
premise: Ulyana Yarrow, the parish's discreet estate lawyer, is handed a will that predates the funeral by a week and names a beneficiary no record can confirm. A confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the burial, hinting that the town's beloved patriarch was murdered and that the proof lies in a ledger hidden in plain sight among his own charitable accounts. As Ulyana decodes it, every ally they trusted — the vicar, the constable, their own mentor — turns out to be protecting a version of events that keeps them complicit. In the end Ulyana must choose between exposing the truth, which destroys the parish and the person they love, or burying the ledger as their predecessors did; they choose truth, but at the cost of the relationship and the town's peace.
about_author: Quentin Vane is the pen name of a former rural solicitor who spent a decade handling wills, probate disputes, and the quiet cruelties of English village life. They write mysteries from a converted tithe barn, drawing on case files they were never allowed to discuss.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ulyana Yarrow's POV. Three days after Edmund Hallow's funeral, a second will surfaces in Ulyana's filing cabinet, dated a week before the first, naming an unknown beneficiary, 'M.V.' Ulyana's careful, alphabetized world tilts. Beat: unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: A confession letter arrives, postmarked the day after the funeral, unsigned: 'I did what the parish required. The ledger knows.' Ulyana recognizes the handwriting as Edmund's. Beat: dread; the dead are speaking.

chapters.title: Filing and Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Ulyana reviews three years of parish legal work, realizing how many oddities they filed without question. Flashbacks to Edmund as a client. Beat: complicity dawning.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Kindness
chapters.summary: Vicar Ruth Ellery warns Ulyana gently to let the estate settle quietly. Her warmth feels like a leash. Beat: first hint that kindness is a tool of power.

chapters.title: Constable Brack's Short List
chapters.summary: Constable Brack interviews Ulyana about the missing first will. He is courteous, thorough, and lying about his timeline. Beat: Ulyana realizes the law here serves the parish, not justice.

chapters.title: M.V.
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the mysterious beneficiary to a defunct children's home Edmund funded. Records were burned in a fire no one discusses. Beat: grief for the erased.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: In Edmund's charitable accounts, Ulyana spots a pattern: entries balanced to the penny for forty years, too perfect. The ledger is encoded in the accounts themselves. Beat: intellectual thrill.

chapters.title: An Old Flame Returns
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes, Ulyana's former lover and Edmund's estranged godson, arrives claiming M.V. is his mother. His return reopens old wounds and old love. Beat: longing against suspicion.

chapters.title: The Fire of '89
chapters.summary: Ulyana digs into the children's home fire that killed four and erased records. Official report contradicts survivor testimony Ulyana once notarized. Beat: horror at institutional rot.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Elders
chapters.summary: The parish's powerful families host Ulyana, flattering, probing, warning. Power is served like dessert. Beat: claustrophobic civility.

chapters.title: First Decoded Entry
chapters.summary: Ulyana cracks the ledger's key — dates matched to hymn numbers — and finds payments labeled 'quieting.' Beat: triumph curdling into nausea.

chapters.title: Tomas's Alibi
chapters.summary: Tomas claims he was abroad when Edmund died; Ulyana verifies it — and discovers he lied about something smaller. Beat: love tested by doubt.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Sermon
chapters.summary: Ruth preaches on loyalty and truth, looking directly at Ulyana. Half the congregation understands the sermon as a threat. Beat: public pressure, private terror.

chapters.title: A Break-In, Tidily Done
chapters.summary: Ulyana's office is searched; nothing stolen, files reordered alphabetically — someone fluent in Ulyana's own system. Beat: violation by one's own mirror.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Advice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's old mentor, solicitor Ada Crane, advises burying the letter: 'Some wills exist so the living can sleep.' Beat: the temptation of inherited silence.

chapters.title: Survivor at the Gate
chapters.summary: A home survivor, elderly Nell Pask, approaches Ulyana with a fragment of the original ledger page. She has waited thirty years to be believed. Beat: moral weight becomes personal.

chapters.title: Brack's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Brack reveals he knows about the letter — and offers to lose it. His protection is a bribe. Beat: corruption wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: What Edmund Loved
chapters.summary: Ulyana reconstructs Edmund's private life: a hidden long love, M.V.'s true identity as his child placed in the home he funded — and failed. Beat: sympathy complicating judgment.

chapters.title: The Quietings Continue
chapters.summary: Decoded entries show the payments never stopped after the fire; they fund current parish projects — including Ruth's food bank. Beat: the rot is alive and well-fed.

chapters.title: Tomas Confesses a Little
chapters.summary: Tomas admits he came for the inheritance, not justice, and asks Ulyana to walk away with him. Beat: love against duty, made literal.

chapters.title: Ada's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana finds Ada's own copy of the pattern in her mentor's archives — Ada has known for decades and helped bury it. Beat: betrayal by the person who taught Ulyana the trade.

chapters.title: Nell's Testimony, Recorded
chapters.summary: Ulyana records Nell's full account. That night, Nell's cottage burns. She survives; the recording is stolen. Beat: the stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: Brack Chooses a Side
chapters.summary: Brack, shaken by the arson, quietly gives Ulyana the fire marshal's sealed report: the '89 fire was set from inside the parish office. Beat: a defection, grudging and costly.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Ruth admits the parish has 'kept peace' with hush money for generations — and that she believes she is saving souls, not buying silence. Beat: the antagonist's sincere conviction.

chapters.title: The Second Will's Witness
chapters.summary: Ulyana tracks the second will's witness to a hospice nurse who confirms Edmund signed it lucid, terrified, naming his child. Beat: the legal thread tightens.

chapters.title: Tomas Disappears
chapters.summary: Tomas vanishes after confronting the elders. His room is stripped; a single decoded ledger page left behind like a message. Beat: fear that love has become leverage.

chapters.title: The Elders' Offer
chapters.summary: The parish families offer Ulyana a partnership, a house, a future — contingent on the letter's 'misplacement.' Beat: power's corruption offered as a gift.

chapters.title: Ulyana Refuses
chapters.summary: Ulyana declines publicly at the parish council, reading one decoded entry aloud. The room's silence is a verdict. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Retaliation, Legal and Otherwise
chapters.summary: Ulyana's license is threatened with a disciplinary complaint; clients withdraw; a brick through the window. Beat: isolation, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: What Brack Buried
chapters.summary: Brack hands over his predecessor's unsent resignation — proof the constabulary has policed the parish's secrets for forty years. Beat: institutions indicted.

chapters.title: Finding Tomas
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces Tomas to a safehouse arranged by Ruth — protection or hostage-keeping, unclear. Their reunion is tender and mistrustful. Beat: love surviving suspicion by a thread.

chapters.title: The Full Ledger Decoded
chapters.summary: Working through the night, Ulyana completes the decode: names, payments, two deaths ruled accidental, and Edmund's final entry — his own confession and instruction to publish. Beat: the truth, whole and heavy.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Ruth admits she posted Edmund's letter a day after the funeral, as he asked — she is the 'parish required,' and she cannot let it end the parish. Beat: antagonist and believer in one body.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Ruth offers Ulyana the choice plainly: publish and destroy Nell's community, Tomas's inheritance, the parish's good works — or seal it and keep the peace. Beat: the theme made a single decision.

chapters.title: Tomas's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Tomas gives Ulyana an ultimatum: leave with him tonight or lose him. Ulyana chooses the ledger. Beat: love against duty, resolved in loss.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ulyana reads both wills at a public probate hearing, presenting the decoded ledger and Nell's sworn statement. The room breaks — elders, constable, vicar all implicated. Beat: climax, truth spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Investigations begin; the good works collapse with the corruption that funded them, hurting the innocent. Ruth resigns and turns herself in. Beat: victory with a bitter taste.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Lost
chapters.summary: Tomas leaves without goodbye. Ada disowns Ulyana professionally. The town is colder, cleaner, awake. Beat: the cost itemized.

chapters.title: Nell's Garden
chapters.summary: Ulyana helps Nell plant a memorial garden for the four children of the fire. The parish, for once, watches in silence that is not complicity. Beat: mourning made public and shared.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Parish
chapters.summary: Months later, Ulyana reopens the office, new files unalphabetized, a letter on the desk from another town asking for help. The dead, it seems, write often. Beat: resolution and continuation — the truth-teller's vocation chosen.
